title: There's a Planet Where It Rains Liquid Iron (4,350 Degrees)

scenes.text: There's a planet where it rains liquid iron.
It's called WASP seventy six b, about six hundred and forty light years away.
Its day side reaches about twenty four hundred degrees Celsius, hot enough to vaporise iron.
Winds carry that iron vapour to the cooler night side.
There it condenses into clouds and falls as drops of liquid metal.
Astronomers spotted this in 2020, on a world with a year shorter than two Earth days.

description:
On the exoplanet WASP-76b, iron vaporises on the scorching day side and rains down as liquid metal on the night side.
The planet is about 640 light-years away and orbits its star in under two Earth days.
Would you ever visit a world like this? Comment below.
first_comment: Iron falls as rain on the night side of WASP-76b. If you could watch it from orbit, what do you think it would look like?
